headline: Israeli fire kills father and 13-year-old son in Gaza on Tuesday
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the killings] Israeli forces killed at least three Palestinians in Gaza on Tuesday Nov 10, local health officials said (Reuters): Fadi Rajab and his 13-year-old son Abubakr were killed in an airstrike that hit the roof of a displacement shelter in the Zeitoun neighbourhood of…
sources: Reuters (citing local health officials/medics); Press TV; Anadolu Agency
fault_line: Ceasefire in name only -- 1,600+ killed since the truce began: is this a ceasefire being violated, or a war that never stopped?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the killings] Israeli forces killed at least three Palestinians in Gaza on Tuesday Nov 10, local health officials said (Reuters): Fadi Rajab and his 13-year-old son Abubakr were killed in an airstrike that hit the roof of a displacement shelter in the Zeitoun neighbourhood of Gaza City; a third person was killed by gunfire in Khan Younis. The Israeli military did not immediately comment. [VERIFIED FACT -- the tolls, scopes kept separate] At least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the Oct 10, 2025 ceasefire (Reuters, citing territory health officials); Gaza Health Ministry's own count is 1,613 killed / 5,833 wounded since the ceasefire (Anadolu, Nov 10; same Nov 9 bulletin recorded at 2100-02 Nov 9). Total killed since Oct 7, 2023: more than 74,000 (Reuters) / 74,643 (Press TV). [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- the day's wider toll] Press TV (09:15 GMT): one Palestinian killed and 17 wounded in Israeli attacks across Gaza since dawn Tuesday; the dead man named as Wahib Khalil Badr al-Adham, killed in an airstrike near Abu Sharikh roundabout, west of Jabalia; seven wounded in a strike on al-Thalathini Street, Gaza City. Anadolu: two more Palestinians wounded Tuesday, including a fisherman shot by Israeli naval forces off Khan Younis. [CONTEXT] Negotiators have failed to agree on Hamas disarmament or Israeli withdrawal; Israeli troops control about two-thirds of the territory (Reuters). Israel says Hamas is trying to regroup; Hamas says it is committed to the ceasefire.
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct tiered publisher families: Reuters (T1) + Press TV (T3, STATE IR) + Anadolu Agency (T3, STATE TR).
sections.what_disputed: (a) The Israeli military did not immediately comment on either incident (Reuters) -- strike attribution rests on medics/health officials. (b) The day's sub-counts come from different outlets at different hours (Press TV 1 killed + 17 wounded since dawn; Reuters 3 killed; Anadolu 2 wounded) and describe different victims/incidents -- do NOT add them into a single 'today' total. (c) Toll scope: post-ceasefire 1,600/1,613 is NOT the total war toll (>74,000); the two figures must never be mixed (2026-10-28 lock).
sections.why_matters: A father and his 13-year-old son, killed on the roof of a displacement shelter in Zeitoun -- a year into a 'ceasefire' that has now killed more than 1,600 Palestinians. The ceasefire holds on paper; in Gaza it kills more people every day. The question is what the word ceasefire still means.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Press TV 09:15 GMT = 13:15 ; Reuters crawled 11:50 UTC = 15:50 ; not recorded) -- Israeli fire kills father and 13-year-old son in Gaza on Tuesday; post-ceasefire toll now at least 1,600

totw_analysis: Our read: A father and his 13-year-old son, killed on the roof of a displacement shelter in Zeitoun -- a year into a 'ceasefire' that has now killed more than 1,600 Palestinians. The ceasefire holds on paper; in Gaza it kills more people every day. The question is what the word ceasefire still means. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Ceasefire in name only -- 1,600+ killed since the truce began: is this a ceasefire being violated, or a war that never stopped?
